title: Calibration & cross-precision throughput/latency study for long-context batching (FP8 vs INT8)
creator: Sofia Nakamura
description:
Goal: Evaluate production viability of FP8 and INT8 quantized model variants for long-context workloads where batching behavior and KV cache warmup interact with tail latency. Deliver a calibration workflow that preserves accuracy within defined thresholds while maximizing tokens/sec under realistic request mixes (single-request long-context, batched short requests, and mixed microbursts).

Scope:
- Quantization targets: FP8 (E4M3 and E5M2 variants) and INT8 (per-tensor and per-channel calibration).
- Tasks: implement calibration runs, run accuracy validation suites, full throughput/latency benchmarks across batch sizes, sequence lengths (512, 2048, 4096), and request arrival patterns (steady, microburst, mixed).
- Measure: token/sec, p50/p95/p99 token latency, model-quality deltas on evals (perplexity on long-context PTB-Long and Wikitext-Long, answer accuracy on long-context QA subset), and degradation modes when KV cache warms up or kernel fallback occurs.

Success criteria:
1) Identify at least one INT8 and one FP8 configuration that: (a) yield >=1.6x tokens/sec vs baseline FP16 for 2048–4096 contexts with batching enabled, and (b) maintain <=1.5% relative drop on pooled accuracy metrics vs FP16 baseline.
2) Produce a documented calibration workflow (scripts + runbook) that can be reproduced by SRE and model-onboarding teams.
3) Provide config recommendations for default runtime policies (batch window, max batch size, KV prewarm heuristics) to avoid >2x tail-latency regression under microbursts.

Methodology summary:
- Calibration: run per-layer activation-range collection on in-distribution long-context slices (sampled from internal long-doc corpora), compare per-channel vs per-tensor for INT8; test symmetric vs asymmetric clipping for FP8. Use reservoir sampling to conserve memory during calibration.
- Accuracy validation: run full eval suite (PPL, QA F1, semantic-sim BLEU where applicable) and targeted long-context hallucination probes.
- Benchmarks: run end-to-end inference harness across the serving fleet image (runtime-1.20) capturing KV cache hit-rate traces and kernel fallback events; simulate arrival patterns using Poisson and Pareto microburst generators; collect token-level latencies via tracing hooks.
- Environment: dedicated lab cluster with A100-80GB and H100 nodes; tests run on both to detect kernel/driver-induced variance.

Risks and mitigations:
- Accuracy regressions concentrated in long-range attention saturation — mitigation: fallback to per-layer mixed-precision for flagged layers and add a calibration pass for attention projection weights.
- Kernel fallback due to memory pressure in large batches — mitigation: test aggressive kv coalescing and batch-size caps; instrument runtime to surface fallback triggers to dashboards.

Deliverables:
- Calibration scripts and a reproducible pipeline on CI (Jenkins job + S3 artifacts).
- Benchmark CSVs and consolidated dashboard comparing variants.
- A brief PRD outlining recommended default runtime config for quantized workloads and a follow-up ENG task to add automatic variant routing policies.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible calibration pipeline checked into runtime-quantization repo with example config for FP8/INT8
Benchmark dashboard (DataDog link) showing tokens/sec and p95/p99 for FP16, INT8(per-channel), INT8(per-tensor), FP8-E4M3, FP8-E5M2 across target contexts
Documented decision: choose production-safe quant variants with justification and expected SLO impact
Runbook describing KV prewarm knobs and batching/window defaults to minimize tail-latency under mixed workloads
notes: 2025-01-12: Kickoff meeting — agreed to include H100 and A100 runs and to prioritize per-channel INT8 calibration to try and reduce accuracy impact for long context.

2025-01-17: First calibration pass complete for INT8 per-tensor and per-channel on model-v2.3; artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-quant-artifacts/ENG-160451/calib-run-20250117/; initial per-channel preserved perplexity better (~0.8% delta) compared to per-tensor (~2.6% delta) on PTB-Long sample.

2025-01-20: FP8-E4M3 variant produced 1.9x tokens/sec in steady batched runs for seq=2048 but showed a 3.4% PPL regression on Wikitext-Long; FP8-E5M2 improved accuracy but reduced throughput benefit to ~1.5x.

2025-01-23: Microburst simulation revealed p99 spikes when KV cache hit-rate <60%; trace indicates kernel fallback events on H100 at batch sizes >48 for seq=4096. Logged issue ENG-160459 to investigate kernel memory accounting and fallback heuristics.

2025-01-28: Decision: default runtime policy for quantized variants will enable small-batch mixed-precision fallback (FP16 for attention projections) when sequence>3072 and batch>32 to cap p99 growth; documented in the PRD draft.
2025-01-30: PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1294 — adds calibration harness and per-channel INT8 pipeline; reviewers: @jamie-chen (SRE), @rahul-m (ML infra).

2025-02-02: Review feedback from ML Infra: calibrations should include a second-stability pass with perturbed sample seeds; added to follow-up tasks. Also requested more fine-grained breakdown of latency by token position (prefix vs tail).
